MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of the Effective Date by and between Granite Peak Home Goods Co., a Florida corporation ("Supplier"), and Northwind Media LLC, a Oregon limited liability company ("Buyer").

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Effective Date" means August 2, 2025.
1.2 "Personnel" means the employees, agents and permitted subcontractors of a party who perform obligations under this Agreement.
1.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity.
1.4 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which national banks in Seattle are authorized to close.
1.5 "Documentation" means the user guides, specifications and operating manuals that Supplier makes generally available for the Services, as updated from time to time.

SECTION 2. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
2.1 Each party shall comply with all laws applicable to its performance of this Agreement, including anti-bribery laws and the export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States.
2.2 Neither party shall export, re-export or transfer any deliverable in violation of the export control laws of the United States or of any other applicable jurisdiction.

SECTION 3. PUBLICITY
3.1 Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in any publicity, customer list or marketing material without the other's prior written consent.

SECTION 4. SEVERABILITY AND WAIVER
4.1 If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in effect. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

SECTION 5. AUDIT
5.1 Buyer may, on 60 days' written notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit Supplier's records relating to fees charged under this Agreement.
5.2 Supplier shall keep those records for at least three (3) years after the fees are invoiced. If an audit shows an overcharge of more than five percent (5%), Supplier shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit.

SECTION 6. FORCE MAJEURE
6.1 Neither party is liable for any delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, war, epidemic, governmental action or failure of public utilities, provided it gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.
6.2 If a force majeure event prevents performance for more than 30 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected SOW on written notice.

SECTION 7. VENUE
7.1 Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Miami-Dade County, Florida, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in those courts.

SECTION 8. WARRANTIES
8.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards, and that each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its specifications for 180 days after acceptance.
8.2 Buyer's exclusive remedy for breach of the warranty in this Section is for Supplier to re-perform the non-conforming Services or, if Supplier cannot do so within a reasonable time, a refund of the fees paid for them.
8.3 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

SECTION 9. PERSONNEL AND SUBCONTRACTING
9.1 Supplier shall assign Personnel with the skills and experience reasonably required to perform the Services. Supplier may replace key Personnel named in an SOW only with Buyer's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
9.2 Supplier may use subcontractors only with Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
9.3 Supplier shall ensure that its Personnel comply with Buyer's reasonable site, security and safety rules when on Buyer's premises.

SECTION 10. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS
10.1 The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between them.

SECTION 11. INDEMNIFICATION
11.1 Supplier shall defend Buyer against any third-party claim alleging that a deliverable infringes a patent, copyright or trademark, and pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.
11.2 The indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control its defense, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

SECTION 12. FEES AND INVOICING
12.1 Buyer shall pay all undisputed amounts within 10 days after the date of Supplier's invoice. Invoices shall be issued monthly in arrears unless an SOW states otherwise.
12.2 Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month and the highest rate permitted by law, from the due date until paid.
12.3 Buyer may withhold any amount it disputes in good faith by notifying Supplier of the dispute within 10 days of the invoice date, with reasonable detail of the reasons. The parties shall work together to resolve any dispute promptly.

SECTION 13. CHANGE CONTROL
13.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees of an SOW by written change request. Supplier shall respond within 10 Business Days with an estimate of the impact on schedule and fees.
13.2 No change is binding until a change order describing it is signed by both parties. Supplier is not obliged to perform any change until that change order is signed.

SECTION 14. NOTICES
14.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses set out on the signature page or as later updated by notice.
14.2 A notice is effective on receipt, or if delivered by courier, 2 Business Day(s) after dispatch.

SECTION 15. ENTIRE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT
15.1 This Agreement, including its Schedules and each SOW, is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and supersedes all prior proposals and understandings.
15.2 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

SECTION 16. NON-SOLICITATION
16.1 During the term of this Agreement and for twenty-four (24) months after it ends, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

SECTION 17. CONFIDENTIALITY
17.1 Each party (the "Recipient") shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the "Discloser") that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"), and shall use it only to perform or receive the benefit of this Agreement.
17.2 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to its Personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than this Section.
17.3 These obligations continue for two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.
17.4 Within 180 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy the Discloser's Confidential Information, except for copies retained in routine backups or as required by law.

SECTION 18. DISPUTE ESCALATION
18.1 The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through their project managers. If unresolved within 30 days, either party may escalate it to an executive of each party, who shall meet within a further 60 days.
18.2 Nothing in this Section prevents a party from seeking urgent injunctive relief.

SECTION 19. TERM AND RENEWAL
19.1 The initial term of this Agreement is forty-eight (48) months from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term").
19.2 After the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of twenty-four (24) months each unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term.

SECTION 20. COUNTERPARTS
20.1 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.

SECTION 21. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
21.1 Upon payment in full of the applicable fees, Buyer shall own all deliverables created specifically for Buyer under an SOW, and Supplier hereby assigns to Buyer all rights in them.
21.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how, and in any general improvements to them. To the extent any of them is incorporated in a deliverable, Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use it as part of that deliverable.

SECTION 22. TAXES
22.1 Fees exclude sales, use, value added and similar taxes. Buyer shall pay any such taxes that Supplier is required to collect, other than taxes on Supplier's net income, property or employees.
22.2 If Buyer is required by law to withhold tax from a payment, it shall pay the amount withheld to the relevant authority and provide Supplier with evidence of payment within 120 days.

SECTION 23. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
23.1 Neither party is liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, even if advised of their possibility.
23.2 Except for the excluded claims below, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed two million five hundred thousand dollars ($2,500,000).
23.3 The limitation above does not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or to its breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement, for which that party's aggregate liability shall not exceed five million dollars ($5,000,000).

SECTION 24. DATA PROTECTION
24.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Buyer, it shall do so only on Buyer's documented instructions and in accordance with the data processing terms in Schedule D.
24.2 Supplier shall notify Buyer without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours, after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Buyer's personal data.
24.3 Supplier shall retain Buyer's data for no longer than 10 days after the end of the applicable SOW, after which it shall securely delete that data unless retention is required by law.

SECTION 25. EFFECT OF TERMINATION
25.1 On termination, Buyer shall pay all fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination, and each party shall return the other's Confidential Information as provided in this Agreement.
25.2 At Buyer's request, Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 90 days after termination, at the rates then in effect.

SECTION 26. GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State of Virginia, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

SECTION 27. ASSIGNMENT
27.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business to which this Agreement relates, on written notice to the other party.

SECTION 28. INSURANCE
28.1 Supplier shall maintain, with insurers rated A- or better, commercial general liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per occurrence, professional liability insurance of at least three million dollars ($3,000,000) per claim, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
28.2 Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance on request and give Buyer at least 90 days' notice before any required policy is cancelled or materially reduced.

SECTION 29. STATEMENTS OF WORK
29.1 The specific services, deliverables, milestones and fees for each engagement will be set out in a statement of work signed by authorized representatives of both parties (each, an "SOW"). Each SOW incorporates the terms of this Agreement.
29.2 Supplier shall not begin work under an SOW until it has been signed by both parties. Work performed before signature is at Supplier's own risk and expense.
29.3 Each SOW will identify a project manager for each party. The project managers will meet at least every 14 days to review progress, risks and open decisions.
29.4 If an SOW conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls, unless the SOW expressly identifies by section number the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.

SECTION 30. ACCEPTANCE
30.1 Buyer shall test each deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW within 10 Business Days of delivery and notify Supplier in writing of acceptance or of any non-conformity.
30.2 If Buyer reports a non-conformity, Supplier shall correct it and redeliver within 90 days, and the acceptance procedure shall be repeated. If a deliverable fails acceptance three (3) times, Buyer may terminate the applicable SOW and recover the fees paid for that deliverable.

SECTION 31. EXPENSES
31.1 Buyer shall reimburse Supplier for reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses that Buyer has approved in writing in advance, at cost and without mark-up, provided they comply with Buyer's travel policy as provided to Supplier.
31.2 Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days after the expense is incurred, with receipts for any single item above two hundred fifty dollars ($250).

SECTION 32. TERMINATION
32.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW on written notice if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 20 days after receiving written notice describing it.
32.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver appointed for its business.
32.3 Buyer may terminate any SOW for convenience on 30 days' written notice, paying for Services performed up to the effective date of termination.

SECTION 33. INFORMATION SECURITY
33.1 Supplier shall maintain administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to protect Buyer's data, consistent with a recognized industry framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
33.2 Supplier shall perform vulnerability scans of systems that process Buyer's data at least every 180 days and remediate critical findings within 20 days.
